Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma
Bench: Subhash Chandra Sharma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 80
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 12235 of 2022
Applicant :- Ravi Shankar

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Applicant :- Mithilesh Kumar Ojha Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
This anticipatory bail application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 1374 of 2020, under sections 376, 506 I.P.C., Police Station Majhola, District Moradabad.
Facts in brief are that the victim was a married lady and the applicant came into contact with her because he used to go to the house of the victim with her husband.
Relations were developed between both of them.
Physical relations were also established.

When the victim pressed him to marry, he refused and also assaulted her with kicks and fists with other members of his family then he fled away regarding which present F.I.R. was lodged under Section 376, 323, 506 I.P.C. which was challenged before this Court in which protection was granted till submission of police report under Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C. and now after investigation charge sheet has been submitted against Ravi Shankar vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: 1 him .
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that in this case victim was a married lady and this applicant was friend of her previous husband.
As per allegation in F.I.R. physical relations between both of them continued for a period of two years during which aid was given by the applicant to the victim.
Later on, she made pressure on him to marry with her but he refused, then this false F.I.R. was lodged by her.

It is further submitted that since the victim was already married,
therefore, there was no question on the part of the applicant to make promise of marriage with her despite the husband of the victim being alive and without taking divorce.
It is also submitted that the victim is used to implicate innocent persons in her trap by lodging false F.I.Rs regarding commission of rape with her.

An incident of which is that an F.I.R. was lodged against Chandrashekhar who was a police constable by the present victim as Crime No. 53 of 2022 under Section 376, 377, 147, 323, 504 I.P.C. and later on she compelled him to make transfer of property in her favour which was transferred through sale deed on 30.03.2022 and he was also compelled to enter into marriage with her, as a result, on 30.03.2022 marriage took place between the victim and constable Chandrashekhar which was got registered before the Marriage Registration Officer.
He further submitted that other F.I.R. was lodged by mother of the victim against Chandrashekhar to grab his remaining property and victim was the real sister of the present victim.

When he was sent to jail, the mother of the victim made compromise and filed an affidavit before the learned Court that she lodged the aforesaid case on the basis of suspicion and on that very ground he was bailed out.
In this way, the conduct of the victim shows that she has lodged the present F.I.R. for the purpose of extracting the property from the applicant.
The present applicant was granted protection by this Court and he has not violated any of the direction of this Court.
He always made co-operation with the investigation and he is ready to face the trial but on account of process of the Court, there appears apprehension of imminent arrest against the applicant.
In case, the applicant is released on anticipatory bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the trial, therefore, requested for anticipatory bail.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record, there appears good ground to grant anticipatory bail in favour of the applicant till pendency of trial.
